name: H5 Data Centers

profile.reading: Per H5 Data Centers own site, this Cleveland, Ohio facility sits at 1625 Rockwell Ave and totals 351,000 square feet, built to Tier III colocation standard with 2N UPS power and 2N backup generators rated for 48 hour diesel runtime. The page does not state a power capacity in MW. The facility offers access to 23 on-net carriers and the CL-IX, FD-IX, and Ohio IX internet exchanges, and is SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS compliant, with a 100 percent sales and use tax abatement under an Ohio incentive program.

reading:
H5 Data Centers is headquartered in Greenwood Village, Colorado, and describes itself as a national provider of wholesale data centers and colocation services. The operator's own site did not state a founding year or ownership structure.

The company lists 33 data center locations spanning the continental United States across three named regions, a Western region including Seattle, Portland, three Quincy, Washington sites, Silicon Valley, Phoenix, and Albuquerque, a Central region including Denver, Omaha, Minneapolis, Chicago, St. Louis, San Antonio, and Nashville, and an Eastern region including New York, New Jersey, Ashburn and Herndon in Virginia, Charlotte, Atlanta, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Cleveland, two Cincinnati sites, three Buffalo sites, and Tampa.

The registry here tracks 4 H5 Data Centers facilities across four states, Oregon, Texas, Virginia, and Washington. This registry also holds a separate operator row named simply H5, with facilities in Arizona, Minnesota, and New Jersey, all three states named among H5 Data Centers' own markets above, strongly suggesting the same company recorded under a shortened name. That row is being cross-linked to this one via duplicate_of rather than merged, per this assignment's no-delete rule. H5's three named Quincy, Washington sites and Cincinnati and Buffalo clusters are useful landmarks for the facility-level research phase, since the operator's own site names specific counts at those locations that this registry's facility rows can be checked against.
